main.claim: Paste your script, set the text size, line height, width and scroll speed, then start the scroll in fullscreen. It runs in your browser, is free, and remembers your script. Mirror mode is there for glass rigs.

sections.heading: How to use the online teleprompter
sections.body:
Open the teleprompter in the browser you use every day. Paste your script into the box. There is nothing to download or install, so you can start in a minute.

1. Open the [online teleprompter](https://teleprompter.lazur.app/).
2. Paste your script.
3. Set the text size, line height and text width so the words are easy to read from where you stand.
4. Set the scroll speed, then start the auto-scroll in fullscreen.
5. Read along. Press Space to pause.

**Space pauses, and Esc exits.** While the script runs, the arrow keys change the speed and the plus and minus keys change the text size. Try these keys once before a real take, so you know where they are.

sections.heading: Settings that matter
sections.body:
Text size decides how far away you can read the words. Line height adds space between lines, so your eyes do not catch on the line above. Text width sets how much of the screen the script uses. A narrow column keeps your eyes on one short line, and a wider one fits more words on each row.

The reading line gives you a fixed place to follow, so the text moves past it at a steady pace. Change one setting at a time, then read a short paragraph to check the result. It is quicker than fixing a whole take after the fact.

If you are reading a long script, break it into short paragraphs with a blank line between them. Shorter blocks are easier to keep your place in, and they help you pause at the right point when you need to breathe.

sections.heading: Mirror mode and glass rigs
sections.body:
Mirror mode flips the text from left to right. People use it with a glass prompter, which reflects the screen onto a sheet of glass in front of the lens, so the words read the right way round for the speaker.

If you do not have a glass rig, leave mirror mode off. On a normal screen, mirrored text is hard to read, and you will lose your place.

sections.heading: The camera option and your script
sections.body:
You can turn on an optional camera preview to see yourself while you read. The preview is for checking your position and your eye line. This teleprompter does not record video, so if you need a video file, record the take with the camera app on your device or another recording tool.

Your script is remembered in the browser you used. It will be there when you come back in that browser. It does not follow you to another computer or browser, so paste it again on any other device.

pages.description: Read your script on screen with an optional camera preview, so you can see yourself while you speak. Free, runs in your browser, and remembers your script.

sections.heading: What the camera option does
sections.body:
The camera option is a preview. When you turn it on, your browser asks for permission to use the camera. Once you allow it, you see yourself in the frame while the script scrolls. That helps you check where you stand, where your eyes are, and how much of you is in the shot.

This teleprompter does not record. If you want a video file, record the take with the camera app on your phone or computer, or with another recording tool, while the teleprompter runs on screen. Do one short test first, so you know the take works before you read the whole script.

sections.heading: Allow the camera on a Mac
sections.body:
Your browser must have permission before the preview can start. On a Mac, check two places.

1. In Safari, choose Safari > Settings, click Websites, then click Camera. Set this site to Allow, or choose Ask so Safari checks with you each time.
2. Open System Settings, go to Privacy & Security, then click Camera. Turn on camera access for the browser you use.

Apple's [camera help page](https://support.apple.com/guide/mac-help/control-access-to-your-camera-mchlf6d108da/mac) lists the app settings in full. Reload the teleprompter after you change them.

sections.heading: Allow the camera on Windows 11
sections.body:
Windows has its own camera switch, and each website still needs its own permission in the browser.

1. Open Start, then go to Settings > Privacy & security > Camera.
2. Turn on Camera access and Let apps access your camera.
3. Turn on Let desktop apps access your camera. Desktop browsers are controlled by this setting.
4. In Microsoft Edge, open Site Permissions and set Camera to Allow for this site.

Microsoft's [camera privacy page](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/privacy/windows-camera-microphone-and-privacy) explains each switch. Reload the page after you change them.

sections.heading: Read well on camera
sections.body:
Put the lens at about the height of your eyes, and read from a line near it. If the text sits far below the lens, the viewer sees you looking down. If it sits off to one side, you look like you are reading from a corner.

Place the text in the middle of the screen, a little under the camera. Use a text width that keeps your eyes on one short line, and a line height that leaves space between lines. Then read a short test paragraph and watch the preview. If your eyes drift, move the text or the camera until they stay steady.

Light matters too, although this teleprompter does not change it. Face a window or a lamp rather than sitting with a bright light behind you, so the preview shows your face clearly. Sit where you plan to sit for the whole take, so your position stays the same from start to finish.

faq.q: Can I record video with an online teleprompter?
faq.a: This teleprompter does not record video. It shows your script on screen and can show an optional camera preview, so you see yourself while you read. To keep a video, record the take with the camera app on your device or another recording tool while the script runs.

faq.q: Does the camera preview need a download?
faq.a: No. The camera preview runs in your browser. The first time, your browser asks for permission, and you select Allow. If you do not turn on the preview, the teleprompter still shows your script and scrolls it.

faq.q: Why does my camera not show up?
faq.a: The most common cause is a blocked camera permission. On a Mac, check Safari > Settings > Websites > Camera, and System Settings > Privacy & Security > Camera. On Windows 11, check Start > Settings > Privacy & security > Camera. Then reload the page and try again.

sections.heading: Set up your laptop as a teleprompter
sections.body:
You need a browser and your script. Nothing else is required.

1. Open the [online teleprompter](https://teleprompter.lazur.app/) in your laptop browser.
2. Paste your script into the box.
3. Set the text size, line height and text width.
4. Set the scroll speed, then start the fullscreen scroll.
5. Press Space to pause and Esc to exit.

Put the laptop at eye level on a stack of books or a box, so the screen sits close to the camera. Plug the laptop in for a long take. Close pop-up windows and notifications before you start, so nothing covers the text.

Before a real take, open the page and run through the whole script once in fullscreen. This shows you where the text ends, whether any line is cut off, and whether the speed feels right with the laptop on its stand. Fix anything you find, then start the take with a clear head.

sections.heading: Where the text sits and where you look
sections.body:
The laptop camera sits at the top edge of the screen. If the text fills the whole screen, your eyes drop to the bottom and the viewer sees you looking down. Keep the text in the upper middle of the screen, close to the camera, so you read while you look toward the lens.

Use the reading line to hold your place. Keep the text width narrow enough that each line is short and easy to scan. If you find yourself losing the line, make the text a little larger and try again.

sections.heading: Speed and size on a small screen
sections.body:
A laptop screen is smaller than a monitor, so start with a larger text size and a narrow text width. Read the script once at a slow pace and time yourself. Then set the speed so the last line reaches the reading line when you finish the script.

While the script runs, the arrow keys change the speed and the plus and minus keys change the text size. Make small changes, not big jumps, so the text does not feel different in the middle of a take.

If the speed is right at the start but you fall behind by the middle, slow the scroll a notch and keep going. Do not stop to fix it. A steady pace with a few small mistakes sounds more natural on camera than a stop and restart. Keep a copy of the script open in another tab, so you can paste it back in if the page is closed by accident.

sections.heading: Leave mirror mode off
sections.body:
Mirror mode is for a glass prompter, which reflects the screen so the text reads correctly for the speaker. On a laptop with no glass in front of it, mirror mode makes the words read backward. Turn it off unless you have a glass rig.

If you are not sure whether you need it, read the first two lines with it on and then with it off. With it on, the words look backward on your screen. Leave it off for any normal laptop setup, and only turn it on when you are sure your rig needs it.

faq.q: Can I use my laptop as a teleprompter?
faq.a: Yes. Open the teleprompter in your laptop browser, paste your script, and start the fullscreen scroll. You do not need to install software. Place the laptop close to your camera so you can read while you look toward the lens.

faq.q: Do I need to download a teleprompter app for my laptop?
faq.a: No. This teleprompter runs in your browser, so there is nothing to install. Open the page, paste your script, and start reading. Your script is remembered in that browser, so it can be there the next time you open the page.

faq.q: Can I use Microsoft Word as a teleprompter?
faq.a: You can paste a script from Word into this teleprompter. It then scrolls the text at the speed you set, in fullscreen, so you do not have to scroll by hand while you read. Copy only the text, then paste it into the box.

sections.heading: How it works next to Zoom
sections.body:
The teleprompter is a web page, not a Zoom add-on. It has no Zoom settings and adds no buttons inside Zoom. You open it in its own browser window, paste your script, and start the scroll. Keep that window on the screen you read from, and keep Zoom in its own window.

Be careful when you share. If you share your whole screen, everyone in the meeting sees the script too. Share only the window you mean to show, and keep the teleprompter out of it.

If you are not sure which window is shared, stop sharing, check what is on screen, and share again. It takes a few seconds and avoids a script appearing on the meeting screen by mistake. Ask a colleague to tell you if they see your script when you start sharing.

sections.heading: Steps before the call
sections.body:
Set up the script before you join, so you are not typing during the meeting.

1. Open the [online teleprompter](https://teleprompter.lazur.app/) in your browser.
2. Paste the script, then set the text size, line height and text width.
3. Set the scroll speed and read the script once as a test.
4. Start the fullscreen scroll only when you are ready to speak. Press Space to pause.

If the text is too small or too large from where you sit, change the text size with the plus and minus keys before you start.

sections.heading: Camera and microphone for the call
sections.body:
Zoom uses your own camera and microphone, not the teleprompter's. Choose the camera and microphone you want in Zoom before the call, then check the picture and sound with a colleague. If you turn on the teleprompter's camera preview, that preview is separate from the camera Zoom uses.

If you use a headset, put it on before you start the script, so you can hear the call and speak at the pace you set. Keep the script on a screen next to the camera, not on a second display that sits to the side, so your eyes stay close to the lens while you talk.

sections.heading: Keep your script private
sections.body:
The script stays in the browser you used, and it is remembered there. Anyone who can see your screen can read it. On a shared computer, the next person who uses the same browser can see your saved script, so close the teleprompter when you finish.

A practical rule: treat the script like any private note. Do not leave it open on a screen that you share in other meetings, and do not paste private details you would not want a colleague to read. The teleprompter shows exactly what you paste, so only paste what you plan to read out.

faq.q: Is there a teleprompter that works with Zoom?
faq.a: You can run a browser teleprompter next to a Zoom call. This one does not connect to Zoom, so it adds no controls inside Zoom. You open it in its own browser window and read from there while you talk on the call.

faq.q: Can you use a teleprompter on Zoom?
faq.a: Yes, if the teleprompter is open on your screen while you are on the call. Keep it in a browser window you can see. Do not share that window unless you want the people in the meeting to see the script.

faq.q: Will other people see my teleprompter in a Zoom meeting?
faq.a: Only if you share the screen or window that shows it. Zoom shows whatever you share. If you share one window, make sure it is not the window with the teleprompter. If you share your whole screen, the teleprompter is visible to everyone.

pages.description: No single teleprompter app is best for everyone. Compare what you need, including camera, voice and install. Try this free browser teleprompter first.
pages.h1: Which is the best teleprompter app
pages.claim: There is no single best app. Pick by what you need: no install, a camera preview, voice-following, or a phone app. This free teleprompter runs in your browser, so you can try it in a minute.

sections.heading: Decide what you need first
sections.body:
Start with the jobs you need the app to do. Most people need only a few of these.

- **No install:** a browser teleprompter opens in a tab, so it works on a computer where you cannot install software.
- **A camera preview:** you see yourself while you read. Check that the app offers it before you commit.
- **Voice-following:** the text scrolls as you speak. Not every app does this.
- **Recording inside the app:** some tools record the video for you. Others leave recording to your camera app.
- **A phone or tablet:** check that the app is made for the device you will hold up while you read.

sections.heading: What this teleprompter does and does not do
sections.body:
This teleprompter shows your script in your browser and scrolls it at the speed you set. You can change the font size, line height, text width and reading line. Mirror mode is there for glass rigs. Fullscreen auto-scroll runs with Space to pause and the arrow keys for speed.

It does not follow your voice, and it does not record video. It is free, and your script is remembered in the browser you used.

sections.heading: Test two or three apps with the same script
sections.body:
Paste the same paragraph into each app you are considering. Read it aloud at your normal pace and time it. Note whether the text sits where your eyes can reach it, whether the scroll matches your pace, and whether the app asks you to sign in or install something you do not need.

The app that feels steady after three reads is the right one for you, even if it is not the most popular.

Write down what you noticed for each app in one line. Compare the notes after the test, not during it. A short written list is easier to judge than a memory of how each one felt, and it keeps you from choosing on looks alone.

Pay attention to setup time too. Count how many steps each app takes before your script is on screen. If one needs an account, a download and three permission prompts before you read a single line, that cost matters when you rehearse every week. A tool that opens in a tab and shows the text at once is quicker to try and quicker to drop if it does not suit you.

sections.heading: Where to start
sections.body:
If you want a free start with nothing to install, open the [online teleprompter](https://teleprompter.lazur.app/). If you want to use the camera preview, read the [camera guide](https://teleprompter.lazur.app/camera) for the permission steps on a Mac or Windows 11 computer.

If you record a practice take first, watch it back once with the sound off. Check your eye line and your posture, then watch once more with the sound on. Two short passes will tell you more than one long one, and you can compare different apps the same way.

faq.q: Is there a truly free teleprompter app?
faq.a: Some tools are free to use, and others are free only for a short time or with limits. Read each tool's pricing before you rely on it. This teleprompter is free and runs in your browser, with nothing to download.

faq.q: Which teleprompter is best if I need voice-following?
faq.a: This teleprompter does not follow your voice. It scrolls at the speed you set, and you can change that speed with the arrow keys while it runs. If voice-following matters to you, choose an app that lists it, and test it with your own voice before you record.

faq.q: Is there an app that works like a teleprompter?
faq.a: A browser page can work like one. Open the teleprompter in a tab, paste your script, and start the fullscreen scroll. It needs no download, and it keeps your script in the browser for your next visit.

sections.heading: How a team can use it
sections.body:
Each person opens the teleprompter in their own browser. The script is remembered in that browser, so one person's script does not appear for someone else on another computer. To give everyone the same script, copy the final text and send it to each teammate in the channel you already use. Each person then pastes it into their own browser.

If you change the script later, send the new version and ask everyone to paste it again. Old copies stay in the browsers where they were pasted until someone replaces them.

Keep one person as the owner of the final text. Ask them to copy from their version when they send an update, so there is one source to check. Everyone else pastes the newest version over the old one before the next session.

sections.heading: Steps for each person
sections.body:
Each teammate follows the same steps on their own computer.

1. Open the [online teleprompter](https://teleprompter.lazur.app/) in your browser.
2. Paste the script you were sent.
3. Set the text size, line height and text width for your own screen.
4. Do a test read at your pace, then start the scroll when you are ready.

Everyone can change the speed with the arrow keys, so each person can set the pace that suits their voice.

If a teammate is new to reading from a screen, let them practice the first paragraph alone a few times. Most people find the rhythm after two or three runs, and a short practice in private is kinder than a first attempt in front of the whole team.

sections.heading: Run a team practice
sections.body:
Before a live session, have each person run the script once and note the speed that feels natural. Speeds differ from person to person, so do not expect one speed to fit everyone.

If the team uses different screens, sizes will differ too. Ask each person to set their own text size and width. The script is the same for everyone, and the fit is set on each screen.

sections.heading: Limits to know before you roll it out
sections.body:
This is a single-person tool. It has no team accounts, no admin view, no shared folders, and no way to see who read what. It does not record video and does not follow your voice.

On a shared computer, the next person who uses the same browser can see the saved script. If your team needs those features, look for a tool built for teams and check what it offers before you commit to it.

If your team's process depends on a shared script with edit history or review, plan for that separately. Use this page for the practice runs, and keep the approved text in whatever system your team already uses for documents.

Before you roll it out, run one full session with two or three people. Note where the flow broke: a paste that did not work, a camera that was blocked, or a script that was copied to the wrong place. Fix those steps in your written instructions, then ask the rest of the team to follow the same checklist.

faq.q: Is there a teleprompter app for teams?
faq.a: This teleprompter is built for one person at a time. Each teammate opens it in their own browser, and there are no team accounts or shared scripts. You can still give everyone the same script by copying the text to each person.

faq.q: Is there a free online teleprompter?
faq.a: Yes. This online teleprompter is free and runs in your browser, so there is nothing to download. Open the page, paste your script, set the size and speed, and start the scroll.

faq.q: Can my team share one script?
faq.a: Yes, by copying. Paste the same text into each person's browser. The script is remembered in each browser separately, so each person works with their own copy, and changes to one copy do not reach the others.

faq.q: Will the script be there the next time I open it?
faq.a: Yes, in the browser you used. The script is remembered in that browser, so it can be there when you come back. It does not travel to another computer or another browser, so paste it again on any other device.
